title: Headroom estimation cascade + customer escalation (reserved pools & burst limits)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: During a weekday traffic surge (US morning peak) multiple dedicated reserved pools underreported available headroom which triggered conservative scale-down and prevented timely burst replenishment. Customer tenants experienced elevated 429s and 2–20s tail latencies for burst traffic while fallback routing amplified load on cold pools. Several enterprise customers opened escalations; support routed an interim mitigation and engineering shipped a hotfix to replace the headroom sampler logic and add visibility.
timeline: 2026-03-10 09:05 UTC: First alerts from Grafana (reserved-pool-util > 95%) 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC: Support receives high-severity tickets from AtlasRetail and BiomedAI reporting elevated error rates 2026-03-10 09:20 UTC: On-call runbook followed, triage in #oncall-autoscaler channel 2026-03-10 09:35 UTC: Initial mitigation: increase soft headroom floor for affected AZs and enable emergency burst-capacity-bypass 2026-03-10 10:10 UTC: Engineering identifies skew between lease-table metrics and allocator view in cross-AZ leader snapshots 2026-03-10 13:45 UTC: Hotfix deployed (leader snapshot merge fix + metric increment) 2026-03-10 14:10 UTC: Error rates fall to baseline; customers notified of temporary mitigation 2026-03-11 08:00 UTC: Post-deploy telemetry confirms stable headroom accounting across AZs 2026-03-12 16:00 UTC: Internal postmortem draft started
detection: Detected via merged alert set: reserved_pool_headroom_low (Grafana) + sudden increase in 429s for /generate endpoints (Honeycomb trace spike). Support tickets called out 'burst capacity not available' for multiple tenants — pattern consistent with reserved-pool accounting rather than model-serving errors.
mitigation: Immediate: Raised soft headroom floor from 5% to 15% for impacted AZs to prevent premature scale-down; enabled emergency bypass to allow burst credits to be consumed even if allocator headroom was negative. Medium-term: rolled out hotfix to leader snapshot merge logic to ensure lease table reflected live pending warmup slots. Communications: Support sent incident status to affected customers and applied temporary customer-specific route pinning for the largest tenants.
root_cause: Race condition in cross-AZ leader snapshot merge where pending warmup reservations were dropped when a leader changed. The autoscaler headroom estimator used only committed leases and omitted in-flight warmup slots in its calculation. During the surge this caused the estimator to underreport available capacity, leading to scale-down decisions and burst-credit starvation. Secondary factor: insufficient observability—no metric exposed for 'pending_warmup_slots' across leader boundaries, which delayed diagnosis.
permanent_fix: 1) Fix: Corrected leader snapshot merge to include pending warmup reservations and added a reconciliation pass that replays recent lease mutations (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/2783). 2) Telemetry: Added 'pending_warmup_slots' metric and dashboard panels (Grafana) and an alert if pending_warmup > 0 but headroom calc < threshold. 3) Safety net: Implement a conservative headroom floor in the allocator for cross-AZ merges until reconciliation completes. 4) E2E test: Add multi-leader failover test to CI simulating AZ leader handovers with pending warmups.

ENG-314574: Ship dashboard and alert for pending_warmup_slots across regions
ENG-314575: Run red team scenario to validate emergency bypass safety and cost impact
ENG-314576: Update runbook to include 'pending_warmup_slots' check and slashing cadence
post_incident_communications: Support posted incident summary to affected customers on 2026-03-10 17:30 UTC with timeline and mitigation notes. Follow-up customer-facing RCA scheduled for 2026-03-16. Account execs provided one-on-one calls for top 5 customers. Internal blameless retro scheduled for 2026-03-18.
observability_changes: New metrics: autoscaler.pending_warmup_slots, allocator.reconciled_lease_count. New dashboards: Reserved Pool Headroom (per-AZ, leader vs reconciled view), Burst Credit Consumption (per-tenant). Alerts: headroom_discrepancy_alert when |leader_headroom - reconciled_headroom| > 10% for > 2m.
customer_notes: AtlasRetail: experienced 12 minutes of degraded throughput; received dedicated route pinning and SLA credit offer. BiomedAI: reported elevated tail latency; engineering provided timeline and mitigation steps. Affected customers offered post-incident call and credit; account teams coordinating.
notes: Cost trade-off: emergency bypass increases short-term unit cost — product and finance agreed to absorb one billing cycle for affected tenants. Security: no customer data exposure; no secrets were changed. Ops: scheduled dry-run of emergency bypass removal in a low-traffic window (2026-03-22).
audit: Deploy history: autoscaler-2.3.1 hotfix deployed via canary then global 60m window. Rollback plan prepared (autoscaler-2.3.0) and not required. Post-deploy smoke validated on reserved-pool canaries in us-east-1 and eu-west-1.
